text: This shrimp punches so fast the water around it bursts.
It's a peacock mantis shrimp, and its club can hit up to eighty kilometres an hour.
That's one of the fastest strikes of any animal.
Slow it right down, and watch the water.
The club moves so fast, it pulls the water apart.
The water tears open into tiny bubbles of vapour.
Then the bubbles collapse, and slam into the shell a second time.
Collapsing bubbles like these can even flash with light, too faint to see.
One punch, two hits: first the club, then the bubbles.
